# Results — Study 924 (First Cut) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The trade: the FOMC announces
the **first cut of an easing cycle** on day `t`; buy **TLT** (20y+ Treasuries) at the
**close of day t+1** — the study's single, documented execution lag — and hold 1, 3, 6 or
12 months, selling at the close of the last session on or before the horizon date. The
scorecard is **excess of BIL** (1-3 month T-bills) over exactly the same days. Costs are
5 bps one-way × NAV on the entry and again on the exit. Daily **total-return** closes
(`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`), never price-only — a coupon is most of a 12-month bond
return. As-of **2026-06-30** (the partial current month is dropped).*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| TLT (duration), BIL (cash) | 2007-05-30 → 2026-06-30 | 4,802 | Fingerprint `ff993b355f57` |

Also cached and used: IEF (7-10y belly cross-check), SHY (front end, the short leg of the
curve expression), `^IRX` (13-week bill rate, the **proxy** cash leg for the pre-BIL era).

## The non-tape input, named up front

The event calendar is **hardcoded by hand** and is the only non-market input in the study.

- **`FIRST_CUTS` (ASSUMPTION, 5 dates):** 2001-01-03, 2007-09-18, 2019-07-31, 2020-03-03,
  2024-09-18. Which cut "starts a cycle" is a judgement, not a datum — labelling
  2020-03-03 a new cycle rather than a continuation of the 2019 adjustment is exactly the
  kind of call that a five-observation study cannot afford to get wrong.
- **`ALL_CUTS` (control, 31 dates):** every FOMC target-rate cut, truncated at 2024-12-18
  so every listed event has a full 12-month forward window inside the as-of.
- **2001-01-03 is unmeasurable** and is dropped: TLT and IEF only list from 2002-07-30. The
  cash leg is *not* what binds here — the `^IRX` proxy cross-check below recovers the same
  four events, not five.

**N = 4.** Everything below is reported with that number attached.

## Per-event table — first cuts, 12-month hold, excess of BIL

| First cut | Entry (t+1) | Exit | TLT | BIL | Excess | Excess net |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2007-09-18 | 2007-09-19 | 2008-09-18 | +14.37% | +2.78% | +11.60% | **+11.50%** |
| 2019-07-31 | 2019-08-01 | 2020-07-31 | +28.58% | +1.11% | +27.47% | **+27.37%** |
| 2020-03-03 | 2020-03-04 | 2021-03-03 | −8.51% | +0.05% | −8.57% | **−8.67%** |
| 2024-09-18 | 2024-09-19 | 2025-09-18 | −6.20% | +4.36% | −10.56% | **−10.66%** |
| *2001-01-03* | — | — | — | — | — | *no ETF tape* |

Mean net **+4.88%**, median **+1.51%**, hit rate **2/4**. The mean is one trade wide: strip
2019 (whose window happens to contain the March 2020 flight to quality) and the remaining
three average **−2.6%**.

**And N = 4 is not four independent bets.** The 2019-07-31 and 2020-03-03 windows overlap by
roughly five months (2020-03-04 → 2020-07-31), so the two largest-magnitude events share the
same pandemic tape. Clustered by non-overlap, the four events are **three episodes**: 2007-08,
2019-20 and 2024-25. The *t* (N=4) below therefore treats correlated observations as
independent and is **oversized**; it is printed because it is the number a reader expects to
see, not because it is the statistic the verdict rests on. That statistic is the daily
Newey-West *t* on the conditional leg, which is smaller still.

## Horizon sweep — first cuts (TLT)

| Horizon | N | Mean excess | Net | Median | *t* (N=4) | Hit | In-window | Other days | HAC *t* (leg) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1m | 4 | +3.18% | +3.08% | +4.61% | +0.91 | 3/4 | +40.1%/y | +2.2%/y | +1.04 |
| 3m | 4 | +0.42% | +0.32% | +3.71% | +0.12 | 3/4 | +3.4%/y | +2.9%/y | +0.18 |
| 6m | 4 | +3.79% | +3.69% | +7.99% | +0.90 | 3/4 | +8.7%/y | +2.2%/y | +0.81 |
| **12m** | 4 | **+4.98%** | **+4.88%** | +1.51% | **+0.55** | 2/4 | +2.6%/y | +3.0%/y | **+0.35** |

"In-window" and "other days" are annualised *conditional* rates on the daily excess-of-cash
series, not the return of a fund — the conditional leg is invested only 18.7% of days at the
12-month horizon. Every point estimate is positive; **no *t* on any horizon reaches 1.1**.

## The control that breaks the premise — ALL cuts, not just the first

| Horizon | N | Mean excess | Net | *t* (N) | Hit | HAC *t* (leg) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1m | 18 | +0.96% | +0.86% | +0.80 | 8/18 | +0.78 |
| 3m | 18 | +0.54% | +0.44% | +0.31 | 9/18 | +0.60 |
| 6m | 18 | +1.30% | +1.20% | +0.64 | 11/18 | +0.65 |
| **12m** | 18 | **+5.60%** | **+5.50%** | **+1.78** | 13/18 | +0.22 |

At the headline 12-month horizon, buying duration after **any** cut paid *more* (+5.50%,
N=18) than buying after the hand-picked *first* cut (+4.88%, N=4).
Whatever is there is a "cuts happen when the economy is soft and bonds rally" effect; the
"first of the cycle" label adds nothing and costs 14 observations.

**Read that *t* = +1.78 as decoration, not as a near-miss.** These 18 twelve-month windows
overlap heavily — **53 of the 153 event pairs share days**, and 2008-01-22 / 2008-01-30 are
eight days apart — so the 18 events collapse onto the same **three macro episodes** as the
first-cut list (2007-08, 2019-20, 2024-25). A one-sample *t* over them assumes independence
that does not exist and is badly oversized; the honest statistic on the same calendar is the
daily HAC *t* on the conditional leg, which is **+0.22**. The comparison that matters here is
between the two *means*, and it is the broad list that wins.

## The placebo — what a random date buys you

2,000 draws of N random start dates, same horizon, same costs, same eligibility rule.

| Horizon | Observed (net) | Placebo mean | Placebo sd | One-sided *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1m | +3.08% | +0.14% | 2.04 | **0.086** |
| 3m | +0.32% | +0.72% | 3.54 | 0.540 |
| 6m | +3.69% | +1.34% | 5.14 | 0.319 |
| 12m | +4.88% | +2.61% | 7.18 | 0.365 |

A random date already earns +2.6% over 12 months, because owning duration paid something on
average over this sample. The first-cut premium above *that* baseline is +2.3 points, which
four events cannot separate from noise (*p* = 0.365). Only the 1-month window is even
suggestive (*p* = 0.086), and four horizons were examined.

**The placebo flatters the trade, and is still lost.** Each draw takes N *iid* dates, whereas
the real events cluster into three episodes. Independent draws have a tighter sampling
distribution than clustered ones, so this null is too narrow and every *p* above is a
**floor** — the correctly clustered *p* would be larger. That direction of error can only
strengthen the None stamp, never rescue the trade.

## Block-bootstrap CI on the daily conditional leg (12m windows, 2,000 draws, 21-day blocks)

| Leg | Annualised | 95% CI | share < 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Post-first-cut conditional **strategy** (full sample) | **+0.47%/y** | [−2.05%, +3.02%] | 36.6% |
| Same leg, counting **only the days it is invested** | +2.62%/y | — | — |
| Unconditional TLT − BIL (invested every day) | +2.89%/y | [−3.64%, +9.04%] | — |

Read the two rates carefully, because they answer different questions and an earlier draft of
this page ran them together. **+0.47%/y is the strategy's excess-of-cash return over the whole
sample** — it is long TLT on the 18.7% of days inside a post-cut window and flat in cash on
the other 81.3%, so it is the number a portfolio would actually book. **+2.62%/y is the rate
earned on the invested days alone**, the like-for-like comparison against buy-and-hold. The
conditional leg loses to simply owning TLT on *either* reading — 0.47 < 2.89 as a portfolio,
2.62 < 2.89 per day at risk — and its CI straddles zero. Nothing about the timing device adds
return; it only removes time.

## Era split (2020-01-01) and sweeps

| Era | N | Mean net (12m) | Events |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| Pre-2020 | 2 | **+19.43%** | 2007-09-18, 2019-07-31 |
| 2020 onward | 2 | **−9.66%** | 2020-03-03, 2024-09-18 |

The sign flips completely between the two halves — two events each side, so this is a
sanity read, not a test, and it is the least reassuring possible shape for it to take.

**Cost sweep (12m, first cuts):** 0 bps → +4.98%, 5 bps → +4.88%, 10 bps → +4.78%,
25 bps → +4.48% (*t* +0.55 → +0.50). Two trades a year cost almost nothing; costs are not
what kills this, the absence of an effect is.

**Curve expression — long TLT / short SHY, 12m, borrow swept (ASSUMPTION, not on any free
tape):** 0 bp/y → +3.01% (*t* +0.36); 25 bp/y → +2.76%; 50 bp/y → +2.51%; 100 bp/y →
+2.01%; 200 bp/y → +1.01% (*t* +0.12). The short leg pays borrow on the shorted notional
for the days held; even at zero borrow the *t* never approaches 1.

## Cross-checks

- **IEF (7-10y belly):** mean net +4.26% at 12m (*t* = +1.17), +2.98% at 6m (*t* = +1.06) —
  same shape, same absence of significance, on an independent duration tape.
- **`^IRX` proxy cash (PROXY — a discount rate accrued daily, no fund fee, no reinvestment
  timing):** N = 4, mean net **+5.09%** (*t* = +0.56), per-event +12.07% / +27.47% / −8.71%
  / −10.49%. Swapping the cash leg moves nothing, and it does **not** rescue 2001 — TLT's
  2002 inception is the binding constraint.
- **Synthetic control** (machinery proof only, never supports the stamp): with a **+9.0%**
  six-month effect planted after each event, pooling 12 worlds × 5 events recovers
  **+8.55%** with *t* = **+6.93**; on the null the same pooling gives −0.83% (*t* = −0.74).
  But a *single* world's five-event *t* clears |*t*| = 2 in only **5/12** planted worlds and
  **1/12** null worlds. The harness is unbiased and correctly sized — and it demonstrates
  the study's real constraint: **at N = 5, a genuine +9% effect is missed more often than
  it is found.**

## Verdict

- **Signal — None.** The tape offers no evidence that the *first* cut of an easing cycle is
  a tradable moment to buy duration. Every horizon's point estimate is positive, and not one
  clears *t* = 1.1 (headline 12m: +4.88%, *t* = +0.55, N = 4). A random start date already
  buys +2.61% over the same horizon, so the one-sided placebo *p* is **0.365** — and because
  that null draws iid dates against clustered real events, 0.365 is a floor. Both *t*'s here
  are oversized anyway: the 12-month windows overlap, so N = 4 is really **three episodes**
  and N = 18 is the same three. The premise fails its own control: buying **any** cut paid
  *more* (+5.50%, N = 18) than buying the hand-picked first one, so the "first of the cycle"
  label carries no information beyond "the Fed is easing". The two pre-2020 events made
  +19.4% and the two since made −9.7%. And the synthetic control shows the deeper problem is
  not a broken
  harness but arithmetic: five events cannot reliably detect a real 9% effect, so this
  design can neither confirm the claim nor refute it — it can only report that nothing
  survives, which is what the desk stamps as None.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** Nothing to bank. The conditional strategy earns +0.47%/y across
  the full sample against a CI of [−2.05%, +3.02%] — and +2.62%/y counting only the days it
  is invested — both *below* the +2.89%/y you get from simply holding TLT the whole time; the
  curve expression is +2.51% per event at a 50 bp/y borrow with *t* = +0.30;
  and the whole positive mean rests on one window (2019-08 → 2020-07) that owes its return
  to a pandemic, not to a rate cut. Anyone sizing this trade would be making a four-sample
  bet on a macro narrative.
- **What it is not.** This is not a finding that duration falls after cuts — owning TLT paid
  +2.89%/y excess of cash across the whole sample. It is a finding that the *timing device*
  adds nothing to that, and that the sample is far too small to say otherwise.
